kaps_punt: Onderwerp 4 - Waardeer en nadenke, Kwartaal 1. Die uitdrukkingskwaliteite van slaginstrumente in ŉ Afrika-musiekstuk. Klassifiseer verskeie instrumente as deel van ŉ familie of groep in terme van voorkoms, benoeming, hoe die klank voortgebring word en die toonhoogte klassifikasie (hoog-laag). Eie en ander se optredes en prosesse deur die gebruik van eenvoudige skeppende kunsterminologie.

items.bewering: Party instrumente maak klank as jy hulle slaan. 'n Ratel klink as jy dit skud, en ander instrumente klink as jy oor hulle skraap. 'n Instrument wat jy slaan, skud of skraap, is 'n slaginstrument.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Percussion instrument' (sounded by being struck or scraped by a beater, including rattles that are shaken); Wiktionary/WordNet definitions (striking, scraping or shaking). Arapahoe Philharmonic 'Instruments of the Orchestra' gives the same three actions for the percussion family.

items.bewering: Jy hoef nie 'n snaar te tokkel of in iets te blaas om musiek te maak nie.
items.bron: Follows from the same percussion definitions (Wikipedia 'Percussion instrument'): percussion instruments are neither plucked nor blown.

items.bewering: Voorkoms / Benoeming / Klank (slaan, skud of skraap) / Toonhoogte (hoog of laag) as the four questions for classifying an instrument
items.blok: Die vier vrae oor elke instrument
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6 (2011), 3.2.3 Creative Arts, Performing Arts, Grade 4 Term 1, Topic 4 (p. 33): 'Classify several instruments as part of a family or group in terms of appearance, name, how the sound is produced and pitch classification (high-low)'.

items.bewering: Die ngoma is 'n trom van die VhaVenda in Limpopo.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, 'ngoma, noun2' (large single-headed drum of the Venda people); John Blacking, Venda music text on the Royal Anthropological Institute / UCL ERA site (Mu_I_Text2); DSAE 'murumba' places Venda in the Northern Transvaal, now Limpopo.

items.bewering: Die lyf word uit een stuk hout uitgehol tot 'n ronde pot. 'n Beesvel word oor die bek getrek.
items.bron: Blacking (ERA, Mu_I_Text2): 'a large, pot-shaped drum with hemispherical resonator carved out of solid wood'. Hearn World Musical Instrument Collection, 'Venda ngoma drum' (wmic.net): body carved out of solid wood, hemispherical pot-shaped resonator; 'the mouth is covered by an ox-hide that is stretched between pegs around the circumference of the rim'.

items.bewering: 'n Speler slaan die vel met 'n stok, en die groot vel gee 'n lae klank.
items.bron: Blacking (ERA, Mu_I_Text2): the ngoma is the bass drum of the set and is 'always played with a stick'; wmic.net: 'This ox-hide drumhead is played with a stick'.

items.bewering: Die grootste en diepste trom wat die VhaVenda gebruik, met beesvel oor uitgeholde hout.
items.bron: Blacking (ERA, Mu_I_Text2): the Venda drum set is ngoma, thungwa and murumba, called bass, tenor and alto; the thungwa has the same shape as the ngoma but is smaller, and the murumba is a small hand drum. ERA 'Ngomani - by the drums' calls the ngoma 'the big bass drum'. wmic.net set: ngoma 22 in / 79 lb against thungwa 14.5 in / 49 lb. Largest and lowest of the Venda drum set holds.

items.bewering: Die hosho kom van die Shona van Zimbabwe. Dit is 'n droë kalbas met harde sade binne.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hosho (instrument)': Zimbabwean instruments used in traditional Shona music, a pair of maranka (mapudzi) gourds holding hota (Canna indica) seeds, which are hard seeds. Grinnell College Musical Instrument Collection record (Bira instruments from Zimbabwe): seeds placed inside each gourd through a hole.

items.bewering: 'n Speler hou een in elke hand en skud die twee saam. Die sade maak 'n droë klank.
items.bron: Grinnell College Musical Instrument Collection, hosho record (omeka-s.grinnell.edu, item 1829, as summarised in search results; the page itself refused a direct fetch): players typically use a pair, one per hand, and the sound comes from swinging the gourds so the seeds strike the inner walls. Wikipedia 'Hosho (instrument)': a pair, listed under shaken idiophones.

items.bewering: Dit het nie 'n vaste plek tussen hoog en laag nie. (hosho, and again for the kokonratels)
items.blok: Die hosho van die Shona; Kokonratels om 'n danser se enkels
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Percussion instrument': instruments with indefinite pitch, such as the rattle, are distinguished from those with definite pitch (timpani, marimba). Both instruments are rattles.

items.bewering: 'n Kalbasratel van Zimbabwe met sade binne, in pare geskud.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Hosho (instrument)' (pair of gourds with seeds, Zimbabwe, shaken idiophone); Grinnell College hosho record (pair, one per hand).

items.bewering: Party dansers in Suid-Afrika bind kokonratels om hulle enkels vas. Dit is lang rye gedroogde kokonne met sand of klippies binne.
items.bron: Florida Museum of Natural History, McGuire Center 'Cocoon artifacts': Zulu dance rattles and Swazi ankle rattles from South Africa made of Argema mimosae cocoons. Penn Museum ankle rattles 2012-31-30 and 2012-31-31 (Zulu, South Africa): moth cocoons stitched on in rows, rattling from small seeds or gravel inside. Hearn collection 'Zulu cocoon ankle rattles': cocoons filled with sand or small stones and sewn onto ropes tied around the ankle, worn for dancing.

items.bewering: Die danser se eie voete laat hulle skud. Elke voetstap gee 'n kort klank.
items.bron: Hearn collection 'Zulu cocoon ankle rattles' and SW Collections Explorer 'emafahlawane' record (ankle rattle worn while dancing): the rattle is tied at the ankle and sounds as the dancer moves.

items.bewering: Volgens voorkoms hoort die ngoma en die hosho saam, want albei het 'n ronde lyf. Die hosho hoort weer by die kokonratels as jy vra hoe die klank gemaak word, want albei word geskud.
items.bron: Ngoma: hemispherical, pot-shaped body (Blacking, ERA; wmic.net). Hosho: round gourds (Wikipedia 'Hosho (instrument)'). Both hosho and cocoon rattles are shaken (Wikipedia 'Hosho'; Hearn collection cocoon rattles). The comparison maps correctly: it groups by the stated criterion only and claims nothing further.

items.bewering: Die vier vrae is vier ewe goeie maniere om instrumente te sorteer, en elke vraag gee sy eie groepe.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, Grade 4 Term 1, Topic 4 (p. 33) sets out the four criteria side by side, with none ranked above another. Formal organology (Hornbostel-Sachs) classifies on sound production, but the lesson presents a classroom sorting exercise, which is what CAPS asks for.

items.bewering: Al die slaginstrumente saam vorm een familie, ook al is hulle nie ewe groot nie. ... Geslaan, geskud en geskraap is drie groepe binne die familie en nie drie families nie. Die instrumente in 'n familie is nie regtig familie van mekaar nie.
items.bron: The four orchestral families (strings, woodwind, brass, percussion), grouped by how the sound is made, with percussion covering anything struck, shaken or scraped: Arapahoe Philharmonic 'Instruments of the Orchestra' and similar orchestra education pages. This is the standard school convention. Note: in Hornbostel-Sachs the ngoma (membranophone) and hosho (idiophone) fall in different classes, so 'one family' is the orchestral convention, not a scientific category. The sentence about instruments not really being related flags the metaphor correctly.

items.bewering: 'n Groep instrumente wat saamgegroepeer word volgens die manier waarop hulle klank maak.
items.bron: Read alone, this definition fits any group made by how sound is produced, including the shaken group (hosho and kokonratels), which is grouped by exactly that. The block 'Een familie, drie groepe' says geslaan, geskud and geskraap are 'drie groepe binne die familie en nie drie families nie'. By its own glossary definition the shaken instruments would be a family, so the definition makes the lesson's own statement false. Sources use 'family' for the broad groups only (strings, woodwind, brass, percussion), e.g. Arapahoe Philharmonic 'Instruments of the Orchestra'.
items.regstelling: The definition must say that a family is one of the few BIG groups and not any group. For example: a family is one of the big groups that instruments are sorted into by how they make sound, such as all the slaginstrumente together. Smaller groups inside it, such as the shaken instruments, are not families. The writer chooses the wording, but it must not let the struck, shaken or scraped group count as a family on its own.

items.bewering: Luister na 'n musiekstuk uit Afrika waarin slaginstrumente saamspeel. Luister eers of hulle hard of sag en vinnig of stadig speel. Luister dan of die slae gelykmatig val en of iets onverwags tussenin kom.
items.bron: Instructions, not factual claims. They match the CAPS Grade 4 Term 1 Topic 4 requirement 'the expressive qualities of percussive musical instruments in an African music piece' (DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, p. 33). Dynamics, tempo and steadiness of beat are expressive qualities.

items.bewering: Hierdie kwartaal het julle ritmiese patrone met liggaamsperkussie geklap en gestamp. Julle het aksieliedjies eenstemmig gesing en in 'n tweeslag- of vierslagmaat beweeg.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6, Grade 4 Term 1 Performing Arts (p. 33): 'Travelling ... in duple or quadruple meter (2/4 or 4/4)'; 'Action songs to accompany physical warm ups'; 'Short rhythm patterns ... using body percussion'; 'Songs, in unison, in tune and in time'. DBE 2023/24 Annual Teaching Plan Gr 4 Life Skills (Creative Arts), Term 1, has the same items. CAPS lists action songs and unison songs as separate bullets; joining them is a fair description of a class singing action songs together.

items.bewering: Praat nou oor jou eie beurt en oor die ander se beurte. Gebruik die woorde van hierdie les ...
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4 Term 1 Topic 4 (p. 33): 'Own and other's performances and processes using simple creative arts terminology'. This is an instruction, not a factual claim.

items.bewering: 'n Instrument wat klank maak as jy dit slaan, skud of skraap.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Percussion instrument'; Wiktionary/WordNet (striking, scraping or shaking).

items.bewering: Hoe iets lyk wanneer jy daarna kyk, soos sy vorm en grootte.
items.bron: Standard meaning of 'voorkoms' (appearance); matches the CAPS criterion 'appearance' (CAPS Gr 4 Term 1, p. 33). It is true read alone.

items.bewering: Om 'n ding by sy eie naam te noem.
items.bron: Standard meaning of 'benoeming' (naming); matches the CAPS criterion 'name' (CAPS Gr 4 Term 1, p. 33). It is true read alone.

items.bewering: Hoe hoog of hoe laag 'n klank is.
items.bron: Standard definition of pitch; CAPS uses 'pitch classification (high-low)' (p. 33).

items.bewering: Die harde dop van 'n vrug wat aan 'n kruipplant groei. Die dop word uitgehol en droog gemaak.
items.bron: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox and NParks Singapore, 'Lagenaria siceraria' (bottle gourd/calabash): an annual climbing vine with a fruit with a hard, durable rind; flesh removed through an opening and the skin dried. Dictionary.com 'calabash': the dried, hollowed-out shell. Read alone, the entry holds.

items.bewering: Die huisie van sydraad wat 'n motruspe om homself spin voordat hy 'n papie word. Dié wat vir ratels gebruik word, is hard en taai as hulle droog is.
items.bron: Britannica 'cocoon': a case produced in the larval stage of moths and others for the resting pupal stage; Dictionary.com: silky strands spun by an insect larva. Florida Museum McGuire Center 'Cocoon artifacts': 'Moth cocoons are strong and sturdy when dried and preserved', and the South African rattles use Argema mimosae (moth) cocoons. cocoon.org: Saturniid cocoons are very tough and become hard when dry.

items.bewering: Klank wat jy met jou eie liggaam maak, soos klap en stamp.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Body percussion': the human body used to create sounds; core sounds include stomping and clapping.

items.bewering: Wanneer almal saam presies dieselfde noot of wysie sing.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Unison': parts sounding the same pitch (or octaves apart) at the same time; in performance, everyone takes the same line. The octave case is left out, which is a fair simplification for a Grade 4 class.

items.bewering: Oefeninge wat jou lyf en stem gereed maak vir beweging en sang.
items.bron: DBE CAPS Life Skills Gr 4-6: Topic 1 'Warm up and play' is preparing the body and voice; Gr 4 Term 1 lists voice warm-ups and physical warm-ups (p. 33). WCED ePortal dance warm-up resource: warm-ups mobilise muscles and joints.

items.bewering: Wanneer jy jou spiere styf trek, soos wanneer jy 'n vuis maak. / Wanneer jy jou spiere slap maak sodat hulle sag en rustig word.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4 Term 1 (p. 33): 'Active relaxation ... (e.g. tense and release exercises ... to loosen hands, fingers ...)'; key terms 'relaxation, tension'. Tensing and releasing muscles is the standard meaning of the pair.

items.bewering: Wanneer jou lyf of 'n deel daarvan van houding of plek verander.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4 Term 1 (p. 33) separates locomotor (changing place) and non-locomotor (bend, stretch, twist: changing position) movement, and the definition covers both.

items.bewering: Om skielik op te hou beweeg en doodstil in jou houding te bly.
items.bron: CAPS Gr 4 Term 1 (p. 33): 'Travelling ... and freezing'; key term 'freeze'. Freeze in dance and drama means stopping still in a held position.

items.bewering: Die ruimte rondom jou lyf wat jy kan bereik sonder om te loop.
items.bron: Laban's kinesphere: the sphere around the body reachable by the limbs without moving from the point of support. ETFO Arts Dance insert: personal space is your own space, explored by reaching without travelling.

items.bewering: Die gedeelde ruimte waarin almal saam beweeg, soos die hele klaskamer.
items.bron: ETFO Arts Dance insert: general space is a group's shared space; CAPS Gr 4 Term 1 (p. 33): 'general (shared) space'.

items.bewering: Wanneer jy 'n klank, beweging of storie uitdink terwyl jy dit doen.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'improvise': to compose, recite, play, or sing extemporaneously (without preparation).

items.bewering: Wanneer jy al jou aandag by een ding hou.
items.bron: Standard dictionary meaning of concentration (focusing all attention on one thing); CAPS lists 'Concentration and listening games' (p. 33).

items.bewering: 'n Noot wat half so lank duur as 'n halwenoot. / 'n Noot wat so lank duur soos twee kwartnote.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Quarter note' (half the length of a half note) and 'Half note' (twice the duration of a quarter note). Each entry is true read alone, though each is defined only by the other.

items.bewering: Tekens wat wys hoe lank 'n speler of sanger stil bly.
items.bron: musictheory.net, 'Rest Duration': a rest marks silence for the length of the note of the same name.

opsomming: One fault: the glossary entry for 'familie', read alone, would make the shaken group a family, which contradicts the lesson's own 'drie groepe binne die familie en nie drie families nie', so the entry must say a family is one of the big groups. Everything else checked out against sources, including the one superlative (the ngoma as the largest and deepest Venda drum, confirmed by Blacking) and the term's CAPS content.
